text:
Nobody in Philadelphia is talking about the standings this week, and that's probably a mercy at 5-10-5. The conversation is Matvei Michkov. The Hockey Writers ran a rumour of a trade request, Kevin Kurz of The Athletic posted that Michkov has not requested a trade, per a team source, and general manager Danny Brière said the Flyers have "no plan" to move him (via Daily Faceoff). Wherever the truth lands, a young winger our numbers flag as a breakout is playing with a lot of noise around him, and he walks into the loudest building on the schedule.

The Flyers did stop a slide on Monday, beating Vancouver 3-1 to end an 0-2-1 run, with Travis Konecny scoring on the power play off a Michkov feed. But this is game four of a five-game trip, and the bigger picture is rough: 42% of the expected goals at five on five (the quality of chances), and a 3.7% playoff chance. Sean Couturier summed up the trip's first leg after Calgary in a line NBC Sports Philadelphia put in its headline: Flyers "finding ways to lose".

Edmonton is the opposite problem. The Oilers are +23 in goal difference on +3.7 expected; they've scored about 20 more goals than their chances usually produce. Some of that is luck, and some of it is having the two best finishers on the planet. Connor McDavid has a point in all 19 games this season (11 goals, 37 assists). Leon Draisaitl has 18 goals in 19 games and has scored in four straight. Devon Levi has been the headline in net, but it's Tristan Jarry tonight, back from an illness and at -1.7 goals saved above expected so far.

That's the soft spot. Dan Vladar is at .880 for Philadelphia, Jarry at .899, and our numbers project 3.14 expected goals for Edmonton and 2.64 for the Flyers. Colton Dach, cleared from the injury report, plays his 100th game, and Jason Dickinson needs one assist for 100.
headline: Michkov brings the noise to Edmonton, where the Oilers just keep scoring

hunch.text: With Michkov's name in every headline this week, our hunch is he answers the only way that ends a news cycle: a goal in Edmonton.
